findings.title: Installer identity check is skipped on first install
findings.body: The new GitHub-user check never runs when Integration.DoesNotExist is raised: dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately. OAuthLoginView only stores github_authenticated_user in pipeline state; build_integration never compares that login to the installer. GitHub's post-install redirect and the installation webhook are unordered, and installation ids are not secret, so an attacker who completes OAuth as themselves and supplies a victim installation_id before the Integration row exists binds that installation to their Sentry org with no sender check. The control the PR describes only runs on the narrow reinstall path where an ACTIVE Integration already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration. Fail closed until the installer identity is known (or compare against the installation record) before calling next_step().

findings.title: Missing sender metadata crashes instead of failing the install
findings.body: The mismatch check indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no guard. Integrations created before this change, or created by build_integration when state has no sender, often have no sender key (or a non-dict sender). On the reinstall path where the Integration row exists but no OrganizationIntegration does, that raises KeyError and the request 500s instead of rendering the invalid-installation page. A missing or malformed sender should be treated as a failed authenticity check.

findings.title: Installation-not-found test now fails on a bogus OAuth state
findings.body: test_installation_not_found still stubs GET /app/installations/{id} as 404, but the follow-up request uses state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which is not the pipeline signature asserted elsewhere (9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3). OAuthLoginView rejects that state and returns "Invalid installation request." before build_integration ever runs, so the test no longer covers the 404 path and would still pass if that error handling regressed. The same generic error string means test_github_user_mismatch also cannot tell a state mismatch from a real sender mismatch. Drive a matching state (and a distinct assertion) through the 404 and user-mismatch cases.
